headline: 75,000 depositors seek to withdraw nearly Tk 4,000cr from Sammilito Islami Bank
summary: Sammilito Islami Bank, formed by merging five troubled Islamic banks, is now processing withdrawal requests. The Bangladesh Bank has provided Tk 5,000 crore to ensure payments and restore depositor confidence.
details: Around 75,000 customers have applied to withdraw their deposits from Sammilito Islami Bank in the first four days of this month. The applicants have sought a total of Tk 3,925 crore, according to bank officials. Sammilito Islami Bank, formed last year by merging five troubled Islamic banks, began disbursing the money today.

The Bangladesh Bank (BB) on Sunday provided Tk 5,000 crore to facilitate payments to customers of the five banks: First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, and EXIM Bank. This liquidity support from the central bank aims to help the newly formed bank meet customer withdrawal demands and resume normal banking operations.

The payment initiative is specifically designed to restore confidence among depositors of the merged banks. These institutions had previously faced severe liquidity and governance problems. The central bank has also announced a scheme to repay the entire amount to depositors in phases.

On August 25, the BB confirmed that there would be no "haircut" on the deposits of customers of Sammilito Islami Bank. Concurrently, it announced that individual depositors would be allowed to withdraw the principal amount of their deposits according to their needs, starting from September 1.

Following this announcement, Sammilito Islami Bank began accepting applications from customers, continuing the process until Sunday. Customers were required to visit their respective branches or sub-branches to submit their applications. Bank officials stated they would verify all applications before handing over the money to depositors.

headline: Five dead after Amazon cargo plane overshoots Miami runway, crashes into vehicles and catches fire
summary: An Amazon Prime Air cargo plane crashed after overshooting a runway at Miami International Airport, resulting in five fatalities and multiple injuries. The incident led to a complex rescue operation and significant airport disruption.
details: At least five people were killed and five injured when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway after landing at Miami International Airport on Sunday. The aircraft crashed into several vehicles and subsequently caught fire.

Miami-Dade County fire chief Ray Jadallah reported that three of the injured were transported to trauma centers in critical condition, while two others received treatment at a local hospital. Victims were trapped in vehicles struck by the plane.

A complex extrication was required, involving a technical rescue team to free individuals trapped in vehicles and conduct a search and rescue for the pilot and co-pilot who were also trapped inside the aircraft.

Video footage showed thick smoke billowing from the blue and white Boeing 767, operating as Prime Air Flight 7598, after it arrived from Puerto Rico. Fire trucks quickly raced to the scene to combat the blaze.

A total of 60 fire apparatuses and nearly 200 personnel from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to the incident. Specialized hazardous materials (HazMat) units were deployed to safely shut down the aircraft's engine and control a fuel leak.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) have launched investigations to determine the exact cause of the runway excursion accident. The NTSB has dispatched a go-team to Miami.

Amazon released a statement acknowledging an "incident" during landing, stating they are gathering details and working with authorities. The airport initially closed all runways, causing numerous flight delays and cancellations, though two runways have since reopened.
